visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: A lucrative overnight payout sounds simple enough, but a night inside a decaying asylum rarely goes according to plan.
visibleEditorialCopy.description: An amusement park mogul gathers an eclectic group of strangers, promising $1 million each if they can survive the night inside a derelict former mental institution in William Malone's horror remake.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: Suspenseful and engaging horror with a steady pace and moderate emotional weight, built for easy late-night viewing.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: At an efficient 93 minutes, it offers an accessible, suspenseful haunted-asylum experience that delivers straightforward genre chills without requiring heavy investment.

issueSummaries: description says the mogul promises '$1 million each' and that the group must 'survive the night'. The overview says only that he 'offers a random group of diverse people $1 million to spend the night'. The overview does not say the sum is paid to each person (it may be a shared or single sum), and it states no survival condition. The copy therefore specifies a payout structure (quantity) and a survival-based condition (plot mechanic) that the packet does not authorize.
claudeAdvisory.sourceBoundaryReason: Most of the copy is grounded or is tolerated figurative language and genre shorthand under A_PRIME_PRODUCTION_MATERIALITY_V1. In description, the promise is recast as '$1 million each if they can survive the night'. This falsely specifies a quantity (per-person payout) and a plot condition (survival), which are named materiality categories, and it shapes viewer expectations about the premise's stakes. It does not contradict the source, invent identities, or reveal any outcome or later event, so the severity is MINOR and not SEVERE. A bounded fix would say 'offers a group of strangers $1 million to spend the night inside a decrepit former mental institution'.

sourceEvidence.notes: description: 'each' has no support, because the overview leaves open whether the $1 million goes to each person or to the group. 'If they can survive' also has no support. The stated condition is only to 'spend the night' in the institution. Survival is a stakes framing the packet does not state.

claudeAdvisory.uncertaintyNotes: This is a near-threshold call. 'Survive the night' could be read as ordinary horror-premise shorthand for spending a night in a haunted asylum, and 'each' is a natural reading of an offer to a group, so an adjudicator could approve on that basis. I flag the description because the overview's payout structure is ambiguous and 'each' resolves it in one direction, and 'survive' adds a stakes condition the overview omits. 'Remake' comes from facts.keywords only, and if Sophia treats facts.keywords as valid grounding, it would be fine. 'Eclectic' and 'derelict' were left within tolerance.
